as any world in the galaxy.|Maketh Tua|{{Rebels|Empire Day (episode)}}}} '''Lothal''' was a [[planet]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories]]. During the early years of the [[Galactic Empire]], Lothal was in a state of economic disrepair and invited the Empire to take over the planet's industries, with the promise of prosperity and security. Although many people said the Empire would bring doom, their attempted [[Insurgency on Lothal|insurgency]] failed, while the [[Lothalite]]s, who preached of new jobs and prosperity, were vindicated. Amid Lothal's growing strife with the Empire in [[5 BBY]], however, Lothal became the nesting ground for the [[Spectres]], a small rebel cell which operated from the [[starship]] ''[[Ghost]]''. After harrying Imperial forces and disrupting Imperial activities for at least a year, the Spectres eventually attracted the attention of [[Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin|Tarkin]] and [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]], who tried unsuccessfully to stamp out these rebels. Vader even imposed a [[Siege of Lothal|blockade]] on the planet, but the Spectres managed to slip through and rejoin [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|the larger rebellion]]. A [[Revolt in an Imperial prison|prison revolt]] led to the escape of several prisoners, including former [[Governor]] [[Ryder Azadi]], who would go on to start [[Lothal resistance group|another rebel cell]] on Lothal. The Imperial blockade would come to cause severe hardship and led [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] to undertake a mercy mission to Lothal. However, this mission was a ruse for the [[House of Organa|Organas]] to deliver ships to the rebellion. In [[2 BBY]], the ongoing rebellion led Azadi's successor, [[Arihnda Pryce]], to invite [[Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo|Thrawn]] and his [[Seventh Fleet (Galactic Empire)|Seventh Fleet]] to establish a [[Blockade|presence]] on Lothal. Ryder's rebel cell's efforts to sabotage Imperial vehicles at the [[Capital City]] [[Imperial Armory Complex]] drew Thrawn's attention. Around [[1 BBY]], the planet was under both heavy Imperial blockade and occupation, with her once pristine environment ruined and on the brink of collapse. Almost all traces of natural resources had been stripped from the planet. With [[fire]]s scattered throughout, extreme pollution covering the planet was visible from orbit. Though pockets of resistance remained, the planet was by-and-large under Imperial control and those who remained who had not willingly joined the Empire pressed into service or simply [[Death|killed]]. However, a ragtag group of rebels led by the Spectres spearheaded a daring move which completely expunged the Imperial presence on and around Lothal. For a time, the planet's citizens lived with the concern that the Empire might attempt to retake it, but the Empire was now fractured by the threat of the Rebel Alliance and Lothal remained a free world for the rest of the [[Galactic Civil War]], almost completely recovering ecologically by the time the conflict came to an end. By [[35 ABY]], Lothal was under the control of the First Order, the successor state to the Empire. Following the [[Battle of Exegol]], Lothal was [[Uprising on Lothal|one]] of many systems that [[Uprising against the First Order|rebelled]] against the Order. ==Description== {{Quote|I like the one about the spine trees of Pelamir Gorge. I went there often as a juvenile. I remember the sound the wind made in the tree cones and the taste of the root tea. And the crisp smell of the needles in winter. The forests are all cut down now. Turned into mines and machines.|Old Jho, reminiscing about Lothal before the Empire|}} [[File:Jhothal.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The settlement of Jhotal surrounded by grassy plains]] The [[Lothal system]] was located on the frontier of the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]] and was several minutes away from the planet [[Garel]] via [[hyperspace]] travel.{{Rebels|Droids in Distress}} The [[Lothal sector]] as a whole was located in the "northeast" of the galaxy, on the extreme edge of the Outer Rim, directly bordering the [[Calamari sector]] (noted for containing [[Mon Cala]]).''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' The planet Lothal was varied world with a [[Temperature|temperate]] climate. It was primarily terrestrial, and was known for its [[grass]]y plains, [[spine tree]] [[forest]]s, farmland, long, low, snow-capped [[mountain]]s, and gentle, shallow inland [[Ocean|seas]] of [[Water|freshwater]]. The planet also had prairie wilderness and marshes, the later of which were said to house [[will-o'-the-wisp]]s. Some notable fauna included the [[loth-cat]]s and the [[Loth-wolf|loth-wolves]].{{Rebels|Flight of the Defender}} By the [[Imperial Era]], loth-wolves were widely believed to be extinct but could manifest themselves to Force-sensitive individuals. They were connected to the planet through the Force and Kanan regarded them as messengers warning them that the Empire was doing something "malevolent" to the planet. Besides the administrative and metropolitan center [[Capital City]], Lothal was sparsely populated; other farming towns were located amid the plains and rock formations across the planet. Distinctive conical spires punctuated the skylines of Lothal's plains, ranging in height and often found in large clusters. Lothal was also known to contain several types of precious minerals, including scarce [[kyber crystal]]s.''[[Star Wars Rebels: The Visual Guide]]'' The [[Galactic Empire]] established several factories and mines which polluted and marred much of the planet's previously pristine natural environment. Imperial business even disrupted the planet's varied weather, which had once brought natural wonders such as thunderheads rolling over its mountains and the sound of the wind. Even those who only knew the Empire still came to miss things such as the smell of [[Jogan fruit|jogan blossoms]] on the breeze since the Empire destroyed many orchards to make way for mines. By [[1 BBY]], much of the planet's surface had been strip-mined to harvest minerals for the Empire. The planet was also polluted by Imperial factories.{{Rebels|The Occupation}} One of the coveted minerals present on the planet was [[doonium]], which the [[Mining Guild]] ruthlessly exploited on Lothal, like it had on multiple other worlds.{{FFGXW2|set=Mining Guild TIE Expansion Pack|cardname=Mining Guild Surveyor}} Lothal also had a southern hemisphere which was covered in grassy plains. Individuals and animals could use a network of caves and tunnels to travel from the northern to southern hemispheres. ===Society and economy===
[[File:Lothal_under_siege.png|thumb|250px|Lothal's Capital City under Imperial rule]]
Prior to the coming of the Galactic Empire, Lothal was governed by a [[Lothal Senate|legislative body]] that was based at the [[Lothal City Capitol Building]] in Capital City. Under Imperial rule, Lothal was ruled by a [[Governor]] who commanded the planet's armed forces and political affairs. Several years before the [[Battle of Yavin]], Lothal was governed by Governor [[Ryder Azadi]], until he was arrested for treason.{{Rebels|Legacy (episode)}} [[Arihnda Pryce]] then became governor and was supported by several [[minister]]s, including Minister Maketh Tua and [[Assistant Vice Minister]] [[Sarkos]]. Lothal was also home to several Imperial government departments including the [[Ministry of Agriculture]], the [[Imperial Agricultural Collective]], the [[Transportation Ministry]], the [[Security Ministry]], the [[Education Ministry]], and a substantial [[Imperial Military]] garrison. Lothal's communications with the wider galaxy were handled by an Imperial Communications Center near the town of [[Jalath]].{{Rebels|Rebel Resolve}} Known Imperial industrial operations including several mines in the [[Westhills]], multiple [[Sienar Fleet Systems]] factories,{{Rebels|Fire Across the Galaxy}} and a [[BlasTech Industries|BlasTech]] weapons laboratory in the [[Easthills]] near Capital City. Lothal was chosen by several Imperial corporations as a base since the planet provided plenty of open space for testing new spacecraft and weapons. These factories provided jobs for many of Lothal's citizens. Under Imperial rule, Lothal's previously self-sufficient farming communities were displaced as the [[Imperial Mining Institute]] evicted farmers to excavate their lands for metal deposits.{{SW|url=news/an-nycc-snapshot-of-the-ever-expanding-star-wars-universe|text=An NYCC Snapshot of the Ever-Expanding ''Star Wars'' Universe}} The Mining Guild was involved in some of these operations in addition to the Empire. The Empire's exorbitantly high taxes on all sorts of goods making their way in or out of Lothal had the unfortunate affect of creating a booming black market in Capital City. There are plenty corrupt government officials to be found on Lothal, many of whom take advantage of the situation, forcing some of Lothal's citizens to pay exorbitant fees as "protection money." Lothal hosted several educational institutions including the [[Academy for Young Imperials]], a one-year junior academy in Capital City that prepared [[Imperial cadet]]s for further training offworld at senior academies throughout the Outer Rim. Other known educational institutions included the [[Technical Institute for Agricultural Research]], the [[Pretor Flats Academy]], the [[Junior Academy of Applied Sciences]], and the [[Vocational School for Institutional Security]]. There was also the upper crust [[Phelarion School]] for the children of both Lothal's wealthy elite and the children of Imperial officers. During the Imperial Era, these schools and academies were used by the Imperial authorities to indoctrinate the planet's young people and to train them to contribute to Lothal's economic development. ==History== ===Early history=== [[File:Jedi_Temple_on_Lothal.png|thumb|left|250px|The Jedi Temple on Lothal]] In ancient times, the [[Jedi Order]] launched a [[Mission to Lothal (Jedi Order)|mission to Lothal]] and discovered a vergence amid the tundra on the northern portion of the planet. Establishing a [[Lothal Jedi Temple|Jedi Temple]] hidden beneath the planet's surface, the entrance could only be exposed through use of [[the Force]]. According to the [[Lothal Calendar]], the planet was settled around [[3277 BBY|3,245]] [[Standard year|years]] before [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]]'s rise to the position of [[Supreme Chancellor]] of the [[Galactic Republic]]. ===Colonization=== Settled by ranchers and farmers as an agricultural world, Lothal had an unremarkable early history. As Lothal became established as a sustainable ecosystem for farming, more and more immigrants trained as technicians and laborers flocked to the planet to support the needs of the farming community. As the colonies grew exponentially, the [[colonist]]s established Capital City on the site of the planet's largest shipping port. As the population grew, Lothal's prosperity took hold on the world. During the time of the Old Republic, the stone circles found all over Lothal on various continents had been a matter of investigation. [[Archaeologist]]s from all over the Outer Rim had come to examine them and decipher their origins. Some attested that the circles were proof that a [[Unidentified ritualistic civilization|ritualistic civilization]] had lived on Lothal millennia before scouts had logged the planet. Others surmised that the slabs were of much more recent placement, dragged together by the original colonists for use as a landing area in place of electronic beacons.''[[The Rebellion Begins]]'' ===Clone Wars=== {{Quote|What was it like to fight in the Clone War?"
"Well, I don't think the fighting ever got to Lothal...|Ezra Bridger and Rex|{{Rebels|Relics of the Old Republic}}}} Due to the location of Lothal far from any prominent [[Hyperspace route|hyperlane]], the planet never became a destination for galactic travelers, and was therefore ignored during times of war. When the [[Clone Wars]] erupted throughout the galaxy, Lothal avoided invasion,{{Rebels|The Lost Commanders}} but suffered a severe drought and a [[plague]] which swept through the herds of livestock which grazed across Lothal. As the crops died and entire herds of livestock perished, the economy of Lothal began to crash as the import/export trade slowed. Petitioning the [[Galactic Senate]] of the Galactic Republic for aid, the Lothalian government was constantly rebutted as the Senate was more concerned with the war effort. When the Galactic Empire [[Proclamation of the New Order|supplanted]] the Republic, Lothal once more requested assistance from the [[Imperial Senate]], and were relieved to obtain a confirmation that Imperial relief [[Takeover of Lothal|would be sent to the planet]]. The Empire was interested in Lothal as it seemed to be a great location for an outpost, and so a [[Imperial Survey Corps|survey team]] was dispatched and, at first, discovered nothing of value except vast crops. As the survey team further investigated however, they discovered extensive [[starship]]-building materials beneath the surface along with the valuable discovery of kyber crystals. The Empire had also sent [[Viper probe droid]]s to collect information, which was collected in the [[Imperial Reconnaissance Report]], a document filed by [[General]] [[Jay Stobie]] of [[Imperial Intelligence]].{{InsiderCite|197|Probing the Galaxy: Imperial Reconnaissance Report}} Within a [[Standard week|week]] of the discovery, [[mining]] facilities and [[droid]] factories were dispatched, along with an [[Lothal garrison|Imperial garrison]], and the planetary government sought to maintain sovereignty. ===Imperialization=== {{Quote|Traitors may rear their cowardly heads from time-to-time, but the word "rebels" shall never become synonymous with Lothal.|General Jay Stobie|}} The Empire drastically changed the appearance of Capital City, evicting large amounts of people and demolishing existing buildings to pave the way for Imperial-style structures, and overnight, large sectors of the city were depopulated. These actions were met with mass protests, which ensued in large-scale arrests and crackdowns, allowing the Empire to cement their leadership and eventually establishing a governorship. What began as a simple loan of credits and supplies quickly became a fully fledged occupation. The Empire soon began plundering the minerals from Lothal with no regard to the [[Lothalite|people]], and the environment became heavily polluted as the skies became clouded in smog, and the rivers were filled with factory waste. As the Empire's mission on Lothal became more and more apparent, citizens grew increasingly upset and uneasy about the drastic negative changes to Lothal, which eventually led to individuals and groups to [[Insurgency on Lothal|resist]] the Empire, only for them to be defeated. One of the earliest revolutionaries were [[Ephraim Bridger|Ephraim]] and [[Mira Bridger]], who transmitted messages of rebellion and hope. Despite being secretly supported by several high-level government officials, the Bridgers eventually were arrested and imprisoned in [[12 BBY]].''[[Dawn of Rebellion]]'' [[File:GovernorPryce-TotOR2023.png|thumb|right|200px|Governor Pryce presided over the Imperialization of Lothal]] During the early Imperial Era, in the year [[15 BBY]], the corrupt Governor Ryder Azadi tried to force Arihnda Pryce into allowing him to buy a controlling stake in her [[Pryce family|family]]'s company [[Pryce Mining]]. After Governor Azadi framed her mother, [[Elainye Pryce]] for embezzlement, Pryce sought out [[Senator]] [[Domus Renking]] for help. Senator Renking agreed to help in return for the Pryces giving the Empire a controlling stake in their mines. As a sop, Senator Renking found Pryce's parents jobs at the mines of [[Batonn]]. Pryce herself found work at Senator Renking's citizen assistance services on [[Coruscant]]. After exposing the illegal activities of the [[Higher Skies Advocacy Group]] and [[Moff]] [[Ghadi]], Pryce convinced [[Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin]] to give her the governorship of Lothal, as revenge against Azadi for forcing her parents out of their mine. Azadi had already incurred the wrath of the Empire by supporting rebellious broadcasts made by Ephraim and Mira Bridger. After Azadi was removed from office and arrested for treason, Pryce was named acting Governor, and spent a year on Coruscant learning the skills of her new job before fully assuming the governorship and returning to Lothal. Upon her arrival, she liquidated Pryce Mining after learning that Senator Renking had exhausted the mine's doonium reserves. Governor Pryce later lobbied for Lothal to host the expanded [[Imperial Navy]] facilities for that region of the Outer Rim. Lothal's bid faced competition from Governor [[Sanz]] of [[Kintoni]]. Pryce then convinced her rival Senator Renking to "persuade" Governor Sanz to withdraw her bid. Renking was subsequently arrested for bribery, entrenching Governor Pryce's power base on Lothal. Due to Pryce's efforts, Lothal won the bid to host the expanded Imperial naval facilities, turning the planet into an Imperial center in that region. As Governor, Pryce oversaw the expansion of the Imperial industrial, mining, and military presence on Lothal. ===Further Imperialization=== {{Quote|We want Lothal to be the center of this part of the Outer Rim. That means industry, mining, commerce, expanded youth and military academies... and a powerful navy presence to maintain it all. If Kintoni starts drawing away our ships, everything else will follow. Do you want to live on Lothal the way it was, Minister Tua? Or do you even remember that far back?|Governor Pryce's vision of Lothal|}} Most of the inhabitants of Lothal initially welcomed the Empire's presence on their planet since Imperial investment seemed to promise an economic boom for the beleaguered Outer Rim agriworld. Arriving on the planet, the Empire viewed Lothal as a world rich in resources to power the fledgling government. As the survey team made a quick scan of the planet, they initially dismissed the planet's resources until deeper scans revealed a wealth of ores and precious stones like kyber crystals. When the Imperial garrison landed in Capital City, they quickly began establishing modular mining facilities and droid-run foundries to begin strip-mining the world, destroying the few remaining successful farms and orchards. Almost overnight, Imperial industrial plants and mines polluted the planet's skies and waterways. [[Stormtrooper]] patrols restricted the freedoms of the citizens, who began turning to crime as joblessness and poverty skyrocketed. While some like [[Beck Ollet]]'s family were compensated for the use of their lands, others were violently evicted from their property. Despite protests from local farmers who lost their lands to Imperial industrial, mining, and military operations, Pryce was unmoved and saw these as sacrifices in the name of progress. When the Empire made plans to establish a new hyperspace route to the planet, industry and the Imperial government bureaucracy on Lothal expanded rapidly, in turn leading to significant offworld migration from the [[Core Worlds]]. The [[Leonis family|Leonises]] and the [[Spanjaf family|Spanjafs]] settled on Lothal to work as agricultural scientists and data-security experts respectively. Sienar Fleet Systems established a [[Sienar Advanced Projects Laboratory|test facility]] that took advantage of the large swaths of uninhabited spaces for flight testing purposes. With a weakened planetary government, the average citizen was left at the mercy of the Empire and forced to work on some projects, many with Sienar, others in mines. As the local population grew increasingly disillusioned with the Empire's policies, a rebel insurgency developed on Lothal. Their activities including [[Westhills bombing attempt|planting explosives]] on Imperial mining droids and attacking Imperial personnel and facilities. [[File:Sabine_looks_over_airfield.png|thumb|left|230px|An Imperial airfield on Lothal.]] About six years before the Battle of Yavin,''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates the beginning of ''Servants of the Empire: Edge of the Galaxy'' to [[6 BBY]]. As ''Servants of the Empire: Edge of the Galaxy'' ends one year after it begins, it must end in [[5 BBY]]. Imperial forces under [[Lieutenant]] [[Piers Roddance]] [[Westhills massacre|massacred]] several peaceful demonstrators in the Westhills, who were petitioning Governor Pryce. The Empire covered up the massacre by claiming that the demonstrators were insurgents who had attacked Imperial mining equipment and personnel. One known rebel cell was a three-man cell that included Beck Ollet, a former Junior AppSci student who was angry that the Empire was destroying Lothal's orchards and murdering several unarmed protesters in the Westhills. Ollet's cell was captured after Imperial authorities managed to identify their [[landspeeder]] following an [[Westhills skirmish|attempt]] to blow up an Imperial mining camp. The Imperial-run [[Lothal Bulletin]] proclaimed itself to be the voice of the Empire on planet.''[[Star Wars Rebels: Fight the Empire]]'' About five years before the Battle of Yavin,In ''Ezra's Gamble'', [[Ezra Bridger]] is fourteen [[Standard year|years]] old. Since ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' establishes that Bridger was [[Reproduction|born]] in [[19 BBY]], ''Ezra's Gamble'' must therefore take place in [[5 BBY]]. the [[Trandoshan]] bounty hunter [[Bossk'wassak'Cradossk|Bossk]] visited Lothal to collect a bounty on the [[Dug]] criminal [[Gronson Takkaro]], who owed a lot of money to the Imperial Senator [[Hack Fenlon]]. Bossk enlisted the services of a local youth named [[Ezra Bridger]]. The two unlikely companions were then drawn into a conspiracy that involved the corrupt [[Imperial Security Bureau]] Lieutenant [[Jenkes]], who was protecting Takkaro and running an illegal sporting event known as [[Gladiator Night]]. Despite Jenkes' efforts to eliminate Bossk, the Trandoshan bounty hunter succeeded in exposing the ISB agent's corrupt dealings to local spectators and the Imperial authorities.''[[Ezra's Gamble]]'' [[File:The_crew_of_the_Ghost.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Spectres had a special connection to Lothal]] By [[5 BBY]], Lothal's standard of living had significantly dropped, and once Imperial supporters and loyalists slowly began to have a change of heart. With the environment poisoned and the people having lived in poverty while Imperial officials grew wealthier, combined with cruel behavior and the deceitful offering of assistance by the Empire, outbreaks of insurgent violence and sparks of [[Early rebellion against the Galactic Empire|rebellion]] ensued, and tensions had reached tipping points. Insurgent attacks began on Imperial assets, including large-scale thefts and an outbreak of insurgent violence took root despite curfews and crackdowns in Capital City. ===Spark of rebellion=== {{Quote|We have been called criminals, but we are not. We are rebels, fighting for the people, fighting for you.|audio=Rebels_Fighting_for_the_People.flac|Ezra Bridger, transmitting using a pirated Imperial tower|{{Rebels|Call to Action}}}} The most notable rebel cell to operate on Lothal were the [[Spectres]], who lived on a modified [[VCX-100 light freighter]] called the ''[[Ghost]]''. They were led by the former [[Jedi]] [[Padawan]] [[Kanan Jarrus]] and the [[Twi'lek]] [[pilot]] [[Hera Syndulla]]. The Spectres were part of a larger underground rebellion. The Spectres waged a campaign of harassment and sabotage against the Imperial authorities. Some of their most notable exploits including ambushing Imperial convoys and stealing their supplies,''[[Star Wars Rebels: Spark of Rebellion]]'' sabotaging Imperial facilities and vehicles,{{Rebels|Art Attack}} infiltrating the Academy for Young Imperials,{{Rebels|Breaking Ranks}} and disrupting the [[Empire Day]] celebrations. In addition, the Spectres distributed relief supplies to the displaced inhabitants of [[Lothal re-settlement camp 43|Tarkintown]]. Following the disruption of the Empire Day celebrations and the exfiltration of the disillusioned [[Imperial Information Office]] employee [[Tseebo]], Governor Arihnda Pryce ordered a planetwide crackdown on sedition and dissent. Under the direction of the Imperial Security Bureau [[Agent]] [[Alexsandr Kallus|Kallus]], Imperial cadets and stormtroopers were used to investigate illegal activities, round up criminals and their dependents, and to ensure that the population complied with all Imperial edicts. The Empire even made an unsuccessful attempt to arrest the Spectres with the help of the undercover Imperial agent [[Gall Trayvis]] at the Lothal City Capitol Building. In response to the Spectres' insurgency, Grand Moff Wilhuff Tarkin visited Lothal to put a stop to the rebel insurgency there. After learning that the Spectres planned to hijack Lothal's [[Imperial Communications Center]] and use it to broadcast their own message, Tarkin devised a trap which succeeded in capturing Kanan. However, Kanan's rebel associates staged a [[Action at Mustafar|successful rescue]] with the help of members of the rebellion. News of Kanan's rescue and the destruction of Tarkin's [[Star Destroyer]] ''[[Sovereign]]'' later trickled down to Lothal. Later, the Spectres returned to Lothal to rescue the defecting Imperial Minister [[Maketh Tua]]. However, this was a trap and Maketh was killed during an explosion, which was blamed on the rebels. In response, [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] placed the planet on lockdown and several Imperial warships blockaded the planet. During the [[Siege of Lothal]], Tarkintown was burned down to punish its inhabitants for accepting help from the rebels in the past. As a result of the Siege, the Spectres resolved not to return to Lothal to avoid endangering the planet's inhabitants.''[[Star Wars Rebels: The Siege of Lothal]]'' Slums had continued to grow due to the refugee crisis that had been created by [[farmer]]s losing their [[farm]]s, and citizens being evicted from their homes. One such slum was Tarkintown, which was destroyed by Darth Vader during the siege in retaliation for accepting rebel aid. The settlers were gathered and sent to [[prison]] camps. [[File:MoradSumarsFarm-FighterFlight.png|thumb|left|250px|The Empire took over many Lothalian farms]] Following the Siege of Lothal, Ezra's broadcast trickled down to the Imperial prison which housed Ephraim, Mira, and Ryder Azadi. Galvanized by hearing their son's speech, Ephraim and Mira staged a breakout from their prison. During the escape attempt, both Bridgers were killed but many prisoners including Azadi managed to escape. As a result of the escape attempt and his parents' [[death]]s, Ezra experienced a [[Force vision]] which led him to return to Lothal with Kanan and [[C1-10P|Chopper]]. Their return to Lothal coincided with the departure of the Imperial fleet at Lothal for an assault on the [[Phoenix Cell]]'s forces on the nearby planet of Garel. Shortly later, Ezra and his companions encountered Azadi and learned about the fate of his parents. In [[3 BBY]], Senator [[Bail Prestor Organa|Bail Organa]] arranged for his adopted daughter [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] to deliver three [[Sphyrna-class Hammerhead corvette|''Sphyrna''-class Hammerhead corvette]] to the planet Lothal. Since the [[Alderaanian]]s could not afford to be seen supporting the rebels, Leia had come to Lothal under the pretext of carrying out a mercy mission. She also arranged for the crew of the ''Ghost'' to rendezvous near the town of Jalath in order to "steal" the corvettes. As a precaution, the Imperial [[Supply Master]] [[Yogar Lyste]] had fastened [[gravity lock]]s to the starships. During a skirmish with Imperial forces in the wilderness, the crew of the ''Ghost'', including Ezra and Kanan, managed to fake Leia's "kidnapping." The stormtroopers were surprised by the fact that the Rebels did not usually take prisoners, even wondering why they did. Together with Leia, they then [[Mission on Lothal|infiltrated]] the Imperial depot and stole the starships. Having completed their mission, the crew of the ''Ghost'' departed Lothal and rejoined the Phoenix fleet.{{Rebels|A Princess on Lothal}} Several months later, the Jedi Kanan, Ezra, and [[Ahsoka Tano]] and the astromech droid Chopper traveled to Lothal to visit the Jedi Temple there. After [[Duel on Oosalon|clashing]] with the Inquisitors known as the [[Fifth Brother]] and the [[Seventh Sister]] on [[Oosalon]], the three Jedi had traveled to the Jedi Temple in order to commune with [[Jedi Master|Master]] [[Yoda]]. There, Ahsoka discovered through a Force vision that her former master Anakin Skywalker had indeed turned to the [[Dark side of the Force|dark side]] and become "Darth Vader." Meanwhile, Kanan managed to complete his [[Jedi Trials]] and become a [[Jedi Knight]] while Ezra talked to Yoda through the Force. Together with Chopper, the three Jedi managed to escape Lothal before the Inquisitors and Imperial reinforcements under Vader arrived.{{Rebels|Shroud of Darkness}} [[File:Sienar_Advanced_Projects_Laboratory-SWGA.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Sienar's Advanced Projects Laboratory on Lothal]] In [[2 BBY]], the rebel insurgency in the Lothal sector led Governor Pryce to solicit the help of [[Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo|Thrawn]] and his [[Seventh Fleet (Galactic Empire)|Seventh Fleet]].''[[Star Wars Rebels: Steps Into Shadow]]'' The Seventh Fleet established a [[Blockade|presence]] in the Lothal system.{{Rebels|Iron Squadron (episode)}} Meanwhile, the escaped Ryder Azadi established [[Lothal resistance group|another rebel cell]] which embarked on a sabotage campaign at the [[Imperial Armory Complex]]. This caused the factory to produce a high rate of defective vehicles, undermining the Imperial effort. After the Phoenix Squadron received intelligence from the [[Fulcrum]] operative Kallus that the Empire was developing a [[TIE/d "Defender" Multi-Role Starfighter|new starfighter initiative]], the Spectres Kanan, Ezra, and Chopper joined forces with Ryder's cell to infiltrate the factory. Despite the death of their local guide [[Morad Sumar]], the rebels managed to steal the plans and escape with the help of Kallus. Meanwhile, Thrawn realized that the crew of the ''Ghost'' had a special connection to Lothal and that they were being aided by a traitor within the Imperial ranks. Later, as part of a [[Rescue of Alexsandr Kallus|mission]] to rescue Kallus, Ezra, Chopper, and [[AP-5]] stole a [[Star Commuter 2000]] from [[Capital City spaceport]] and were captured by Lieutenant Lyste's [[Arquitens-class command cruiser|''Arquitens''-class command cruiser]]. Though Kallus managed to frame Lyste, Thrawn discovered that he was Fulcrum but allowed him to continue operating in order to lure the rebels out of hiding.{{Rebels|Through Imperial Eyes}} Later, the Phoenix Squadron and [[General]] [[Jan Dodonna]]'s [[Massassi Group]] planned a coordinated strike on the TIE Defender factories on Lothal. However, Thrawn's spies reported their movements and the trajectory of Dodonna's fleet. In response, Thrawn convened a secret meeting with Governor Pryce, Admiral Konstantine, and Grand Moff Tarkin at the Imperial headquarters in order to lure Kallus out of hiding. After capturing Kallus, Thrawn was able to use the trajectory of his Fulcrum transmission to identify Atollon's location. Thrawn's Seventh Fleet [[Battle of Atollon|besieged]] the rebel forces, preventing them from launching their attack on Lothal. The surviving rebels fled to [[Yavin 4]].{{Rebels|Zero Hour}} [[File:Polluted_Lothal.png|thumb|left|227x227px|Lothal, polluted by the Empire and burning]] By 1 BBY, extensive Imperial industrial production had left the planet pockmarked with areas of [[fire]] and heavy pollution reaching all the way to the upper [[atmosphere]]. Ezra Bridger, returning to the planet with [[Cikatro Vizago]], thought that the planet was nearly unrecognizable and felt that it looked like it was dying. Mining Guild [[ore crawler]]s also excavated the planet's surface for raw minerals to feed the Imperial war machine, razing vast tracts of Lothal's plains and hurting the planet badly. Those who broke Imperial law including smugglers like Cikatro Vizago were forced to worked as slaves aboard these ore crawlers.{{Rebels|Crawler Commandeers}} The Empire also imposed a night curfew in major centers such as Capital City. Despite a [[Raid on a suspected rebel cell|harsh Imperial crackdown]] which claimed the life of [[Jho]], Ryder Azadi's rebel cell managed to continue operating on Lothal and relayed intelligence about the Empire's [[TIE/D Defender Elite]] project to the Rebel Alliance on Yavin 4. Feeling a special connection to Lothal, the Spectres smuggled themselves in Lothal with the help of Vizago, who was subsequently arrested by the Empire for smuggling [[puffer pig]]s. In Capital City, Ezra and [[Sabine Wren]] reunited with an old rebel contact named [[Jai Kell]]. The Spectres and Jai Kell managed to evade Imperial forces by fleeing into the city's sewers and rendezvoused with Ryder's cell. [[File:TIE_Defender_Elite_FotD.png|thumb|right|220x220px|The TIE Defender Elite]] The Spectres, Ryder Azadi, and Jai Kell then infiltrated an [[Lothal Imperial airfield|Imperial testing facility]] in Lothal's wilderness where the Empire was testing their new TIE/D Defender Elite. The rebels' [[Theft of the TIE Defender Elite|mission]] coincided with the arrival of Grand Admiral Thrawn and Governor Pryce. Prior to the test flight, Ezra and Sabine stole the TIE/D Defender Elite and shot down three [[TIE/IN interceptor|TIE Interceptors]]. After crashing their fighter, Ezra and Sabine managed to recover the flight data recorder. While traveling through Lothal's wilderness, they were rescued by a loth-wolf, a mythical [[Force-sensitive]] Lothalian creature, which reunited them with their fellow rebels. In response to the rebel heist, Thrawn dispatched the [[Noghri]] agent [[Rukh]] to hunt down the rebels. Later, Ezra, Jai, and Zeb returned to the crash site to recover the TIE/D Defender Elite's hyperdrive, which Sabine hoped to install on Ryder's [[UT-60D U-wing starfighter/support craft|U-wing]]. Despite being pursued by Rukh and scout troopers, the rebels managed to escaped. Hera and Chopper managed to escape offworld on Ryder's U-wing with the flight data recorder while the other Spectres and Ryder managed to escape to Lothal's southern hemisphere with the help of a pack of loth-wolves.{{Rebels|Kindred}} [[File:Ezra_Vizago_and_the_liberated_workers.jpg|left|thumb|228x228px|Vizago became captain of the ore crawler]] While traveling through Lothal's plains, the Spectres encountered the Mining Guild ore crawler [[Crawler 413-24]]. After subduing the Trandoshan Mining Guild captain [[Seevor]] and killing the foreman [[Proach]], the rebels liberated the slaves including Vizago; who had been enslaved for smuggling in rebels and puffer pigs. The rebels also narrowly escaped an Imperial search party. Seevor escaped but was killed by Ezra. Out of gratitude, the liberated former slaves joined the Rebellion. Hera later contacted the Spectres to inform them that [[Alliance High Command|Rebel Command]] had authorized a strike on the Imperial armory complex on Lothal. Hera led a squadron of rebel [[T-65B X-wing starfighter|X-wings]] on a [[Attack on Lothal|raid]] on Lothal. Despite Kanan and the other Spectres sabotaging the Imperial anti-air defenses, Grand Admiral Thrawn's fleet succeeded in shooting down most of the attack force. Hera, Chopper, and several of the surviving pilots including [[Mart Mattin]] crash-landed in the streets of Lothal's Capital City. Due to the failure of the air raid, Kanan and the other rebels were forced to retreat. Chopper and Mart managed to flee into Lothal's sewers but Hera was hunted down and captured by Rukh, who handed her over to Governor Pryce.{{Rebels|Rebel Assault}} [[File:SWR_Attack_on_Lothal.png|thumb|right|226x226px|The rebel attack]] During the effort to [[Rescue of Hera Syndulla (Lothal)|rescue Hera]], the Spectres were cornered in the [[Lothal City fuel depot|fuel depot]] outside the capital. Determined to kill the rebels no matter the cost, Governor Pryce ordered her [[All Terrain Armored Transport|AT-ATs]] to fire on the depot, forcing Kanan to sacrifice himself so that the others could escape.{{Rebels|Jedi Night}} Jubilant despite the losses, Pryce decided to hold a parade in the capital to celebrate the "victory," and to hide the fact that she had destroyed the entire fuel surplus required to power Lothal's factories, essentially shutting down the TIE Defender project - the entire objective of the Spectres' mission. Grand Admiral Thrawn, who had left for Coruscant to meet with the Emperor, was not fooled, coldly informed Pryce that he would deal with her when he returned, and ordered Rukh to eliminate the surviving rebels.{{Rebels|DUME}} ===Liberation of Lothal=== {{Quote|Whatever happens next happens to both of us..''"
"''That's the idea.|Thrawn and Ezra prior to their disappearance|{{Rebels|Family Reunion – and Farewell}}}} Maintaining the initiative, the rebels embarked on a daring plan to liberate the capital and end the Imperial occupation. Governor Pryce was contacted on a pre-Imperial channel by Ryder Azadi, who demanded amnesty in exchange for turning over the Spectres and their followers. Pryce leapt at the opportunity and led gunships to the coordinates Azadi gave her, destroying the rebel-controlled ore hauler taken from the Guild and managing to capture Ezra, Sabine, Zeb, and the others. However, it proved to be a ruse to lure Pryce into the open; the ''Ghost'', joined by Hondo Ohnaka's crew and former clone troopers [[Wolffe]] and [[Gregor]], destroyed Pryce's gunships, and a pack of loth-wolves were able to subdue the governor and her remaining troopers.{{Rebels|A Fool's Hope}} [[File:SWR_Liberation_of_Lothal.png|left|thumb|258x258px|The liberation of Lothal]] Taking Pryce hostage, Ezra's plan to [[Liberation of Lothal|finally liberate Lothal]] was to take control of the Imperial headquarters dome, lure the Imperial troops into the base, and launch the dome into the air, where it would be set to self-destruct. With his knowledge of Imperial doctrine, Kallus issued [[Protocol 13]], the order for all Imperial forces to evacuate, an order legitimized by Azadi masquerading as ISB Colonel [[Wullf Yularen]]. However, Rukh was able to warn Thrawn of the rebels' capture of Pryce, and the Grand Admiral ordered him to disable the planetary shield generator. The ''Chimaera'' entered the sky just above the dome, which would prevent the rebels from launching the dome without causing catastrophic damage to the city below. Opening a channel, Ezra demanded that the Empire leave Lothal, to which Thrawn replied that unless Ezra surrendered to him, he would destroy the capital and kill everyone in it. Demonstrating his resolve, Thrawn ordered a brief bombardment of the city, leading Ezra to surrender himself to the Grand Admiral. With Ezra aboard the ''Chimaera'', Hera and Sabine directed their forces to take control of the shield generator and raise the planetary shields before Thrawn resumed the bombardment. The shield was able to prevent further devastation of the city and its inhabitants. They also received aid from an unlikely source. On Ezra's instructions, Mart Mattin flew the ''Ghost'' into orbit and transmitted a signal to lure a flock of [[purrgil]], whale-like creatures that could travel through hyperspace, to destroy the blockading fleet in orbit and seize the ''Chimaera''. Ezra remained aboard the ''Chimaera'' to ensure that Thrawn would not escape, as the purrgil took the ''Chimaera'' and its occupants into hyperspace, destination unknown. The rebels initiated the dome's launch sequence and escaped aboard the ''Ghost'' before activating the dome's self-destruct, killing Governor Pryce and nearly the entire Imperial garrison. Shortly after, the remaining Imperial officers and stormtroopers were captured and forced to surrender by the civilians of Capital City as the rebels celebrated their victory. [[File:SWR_Capital_City_Post_Endor.jpg|thumb|right|239x239px|Lothal after the fall of the Empire]] With Pryce dead, the blockade fleet destroyed, and Thrawn and the ''Chimaera'' missing, the Imperial administration on Lothal collapsed. Despite some concerns among the rebels, the expected retaliatory attack would never come. Despite this, ''[[The Rebel Files]]'', a collection of documents that archived the history of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]], claimed that Lothal continued Imperial ship production, though at a low rate and with low security.''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]'' Sometime after the [[Battle of Hoth]], [[Luke Skywalker]] visited Lothal in search of knowledge about the Jedi to complete his training. Although he found a place belonging to the Jedi in the world, he didn't get what he was looking for, as the knowledge was buried underground. Skywalker felt the place had to be opened up with the use of the Force, but the place didn't respond to him since it was destroyed.[[Star Wars (2020) 19|''Star Wars'' (2020) 19]] By the aftermath of the [[Battle of Endor]], the grasslands had fully regrown and Capital City had been restored to its previous beauty. ===New Republic era=== [[File:Post_Endor_Sabine.jpg|left|thumb|220x220px|Sabine on Lothal after the Battle of Endor]] In [[5 ABY]], while en [[Mission to Chinook Station|route]] to [[Chinook Station]] on [[Bespin]], [[Del Meeko]] expressed interest in traveling to Lothal once the [[Galactic Civil War|war]] was over.''[[Star Wars Battlefront II]]'' [[E-wing starfighter|E-wing escort fighters]] patrolled Lothal to keep the world safe during the [[New Republic Era]].{{InsiderCite|225|Launchpad}} Some time after the Battle of Endor, Sabine Wren stood on the platform of the [[LothalNet comm tower E-272]], the place where Ezra had lived years ago. While looking at Capital City, she saw two X-wing star fighters and [[T-6 1974|''T-6'' One-Nine-Seven-Four]], Tano's [[T-6 shuttle]]. She rode into the city after them and stopped in a building to look at a [[Spectres mural|painting]] of the Spectres. Wren then departed with Tano aboard the shuttle to find Ezra Bridger and bring him home. In [[9 ABY]], a celebration was held to mark the seventh anniversary of the [[Liberation of Lothal]]. Governor Azadi officiated over the victory celebration in Capital City. While Wren was scheduled to attend, she chose not to attend since she was still grieving over the disappearance of her friend and comrade Bridger. Azadi instead assigned fellow rebel veteran [[Jai Kell]] to speak in Wren's place. Two [[New Republic]] E-wing fighters pursued her but Wren escaped on her [[speeder bike]] to her home at [[LothalNet comm tower E-272|Bridger's former comm tower hiding place]]. Later, Tano visited Lothal to update Wren about a [[star map]] she found at a [[ Nightsisters' Temple]] on [[Arcana]]. Tano believed that the map could help lead them to Bridger and enlisted Wren's help in deciphering the map. Against Tano's orders, Wren took the map to her tower home. She discovered that the map contained a [[Pathway to Peridea|pathway]] to [[far galaxy|another galaxy]]. There, she was ambushed by the mercenary [[Shin Hati]] and two [[HK-model gladiator droid|HK assassin droid]]s. Wren was seriously wounded during the confrontation and Hati escape with the star map. Tano brought Wren to a hospital where she was treated for her injuries. There, Wren shared her knowledge of the star map's information with Tano. Tano later visited Wren's tower home where she incapacitated a HK assassin droid that had been staying behind. With the help of the [[architect droid]] [[Huyang]] and Wren, Tano discovered that the droid hailed from [[Corellia]], where the Imperial loyalist [[Morgan Elsbeth]] owned a shipyard. While Tano traveled to Corellia, Wren stayed behind to recover. After recovering from her injuries, Wren cut her hair, donned her [[Mandalorian armor]] and visited a memorial to her Spectres' comrades. Tano later visited Wren at the memorial and the two departed to pursue the fugitive Elsbeth and [[Morgan Elsbeth's forces|her forces]].{{Ahsoka|Part Two: Toil and Trouble}} ===The galaxy against the First Order=== By [[35 ABY]],{{FilmDate|IX}} Lothal was in [[Uprising on Lothal|open rebellion]] [[Uprising against the First Order|against]] the [[First Order]].''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: A Junior Novel]]'' ==Inhabitants== [[File:Vizago_Inspects_Blasters.png|thumb|right|250px|Lothal was home to numerous species]] A very frontier-oriented world, Lothal was home to a diverse mixture of species including, but not limited to, [[human]]s, [[Xexto]], [[Ithorian]]s, [[Rodian]]s, [[Aqualish]], [[Gotal]]s, and [[Ugnaught]]s. As such, the world's inhabitants spoke a variety of [[language]]s in addition to [[Galactic Basic Standard]], including [[Aqualish (language)|Aqualish]], [[Huttese]], and [[Ithorese]]. Some humans such as [[athletic director]] [[Janus Fhurek]] harbored [[Xenophobia|xenophobic]] attitudes towards [[alien]] species, who believed that the Empire should ascertain which alien and immigrant species were desirable and undesirable and objected to the presence of aliens in his school's [[grav-ball]] team, but the majority of Lothal's human inhabitants coexisted harmoniously with the aliens. Lothal was also home to several criminals and crime syndicates including the [[Devaronian]] [[crime lord]] Cikatro Vizago and [[Yahenna Laxo]]'s [[Gray Syndicate]]. Vizago and many other crime lords hired [[IG-RM bodyguard and enforcer droid|IG-RM droids]] to patrol the streets of Capital City, and do their dirty work. The sport grav-ball was also popular among Lothalians and was played by two opposing teams. In the Lothalian version of the game, a grav-ball grid was divided lengthwise into eight zones, called octets. The team that won the [[chance cube]] toss started at the center of the grid. They had three drives to move eight meters into the next octet. If they succeeded, they got three new drives to continue for another eight meters. If they failed, the ball went to the opposing team, who played in the other direction. Grav-ball was played during the winter season and several schools fielded teams. One notable team was Junior AppSci's [[AppSci SaberCats]], which won the championship several years before the Battle of Yavin. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|Where Ezra lives, where we meet him, the prairie that he lives on, the city, the town that it's adjacent to—all of that, literally down to what the alleys look like in the town—was inspired by Ralph's original art.|''Star Wars Rebels'' executive producer [[Simon Kinberg]]|}} [[File:RMQ-KillikMounds.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Ralph McQuarrie painting of [[Sicemon]], which ''The Illustrated Star Wars Universe'' described as the [[Castle Lands]] of Alderaan]] The name of Lothal comes from the real-world ancient city of [[Wikipedia:Lothal|Lothal]] of the [[Wikipedia:Indus Valley Civilization|Indus Valley Civilization]].{{Twitter|pabl0hidalgo|status/1597072598268989440|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|quote=Yep. That's what I had in mind.|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/VayOP}} The name came about while researching ancient shipyards,{{Twitter|pabl0hidalgo|status/1597067730498117635|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|quote=Found the piece of paper where Lothal appeared as the suggested planet name for Rebels. I was researching historic shipyards.|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/1y0GC}} the city Lothal being the site of the world's first known ship dock,[[Wikipedia:Lothal]] as the planet Lothal eventually heavily featured shipyards and ship factories. The name was briefly considered for the homeworld of the main character of [[Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens|''Star Wars'': Episode VII ''The Force Awakens'']] who would become [[Rey Skywalker|Rey]], but the worlds were taken in different directions.{{Twitter|pabl0hidalgo|status/1597068894312992768|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|quote=I posted this ages ago, but very early on there was the possibility that “Lothal” would be the home world of Taryn/Kira/Rey but both worlds went in different directions for the better ultimately|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/vWFOm}} Lothal's look is based directly on concept paintings by [[Ralph McQuarrie]].{{WebCite|url=https://ew.com/article/2014/01/23/star-wars-rebels-interview|text='Star Wars Rebels' interview: New series goes to dark places, embraces 1977 film's spirit|author=Hibberd, James|date=2014-01-23|work=Entertainment Weekly|archivedate=20181201233215}} These same paintings were used in ''[[The Illustrated Star Wars Universe]]'' to illustrate portions of [[Alderaan]].''[[The Illustrated Star Wars Universe]]'' After [[StarWars.com]]'s reveal of the planet Lothal and its Sienar factory, a website at [http://www.sienarfleetsystems.com www.sienarfleetsystems.com] appeared.
